projects.title: Dev Portfolio Platform
projects.summary: A dynamic, full-stack portfolio platform with Google authentication, Stripe/Cashfree payment integration, blog support, activity tracking, and an AI chatbot.
projects.problem: Most portfolios are static and don't demonstrate real-world engineering skills or visitor interaction. Developers struggle to showcase end-to-end systems, payment processing, or live user engagement.
projects.solution:
Built a full-stack SaaS-level portfolio platform with:
- Google OAuth authentication
- Payment system integration (Cashfree/Stripe)
- Blog support with comments
- Activity tracking for visitor engagement
- AI chatbot integration (RAG + DeepSeek)
- Admin dashboard for content management
- Newsletter subscription system
projects.impact:
- Demonstrates real-world SaaS architecture and engineering depth
- Handles actual user interactions (payments, subscriptions, support tickets)
- Shows scalability, security (JWT, payments, CORS), and production-grade tooling
- Live platform with genuine user engagement and analytics
projects.realWorldUsage: Used as a live portfolio by Gaurav to attract recruiters and clients. Visitors can explore projects, book services, engage via chatbot, and understand full-stack capabilities in real time.
projects.architecture: Frontend: React, Tailwind, Vite on Vercel. Backend: Node.js/Express, MongoDB, payment webhooks. Chatbot: DeepSeek API with RAG retrieval.

projects.title: Personal AI Chatbot (RAG + DeepSeek)
projects.summary: A production-ready AI chatbot powered by RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) and DeepSeek API. Answers questions about projects, skills, services with context-aware accuracy.
projects.problem: Visitors to portfolio sites don't want to scroll through entire portfolios to understand skills and projects. Static FAQs are outdated. Chatbots hallucinate or give inaccurate information.
projects.solution:
Built a RAG-based chatbot that:
- Retrieves answers only from structured JSON knowledge base
- Uses keyword matching + semantic scoring for relevance
- Integrates DeepSeek API for conversational responses
- Stores all conversations in MongoDB for analytics
- Implements guardrails to prevent off-topic answers
- Caches responses to reduce API calls
projects.impact:
- Instant answers to portfolio questions (projects, skills, services)
- Improves user engagement and time-on-site
- Reduces support inquiries by answering common questions
- Provides analytics on what visitors care about
- No hallucination - answers only from verified data
projects.realWorldUsage: Live on portfolio at /lab/gaurav-chatbot. Visitors ask: 'What projects have you built?', 'What technologies do you use?', 'Can you help with debugging?', 'What's your experience?'
highlights: RAG retrieval from JSON knowledge base
Rate limiting (30 msgs/10 min per IP)
projects.architecture: Frontend: React chat UI with session state. Backend: Node.js/Express with RAG pipeline. LLM: DeepSeek API. Database: MongoDB for conversation history.

- Booking and scheduling system
- Secure payment processing

- Activity event logging
- Automated receipt generation

projects.impact:
- Streamlined client interaction from discovery to delivery
- Demonstrates real business use-case with revenue model
- Shows backend + payment integration expertise
- Built-in analytics for service performance
- Professional client experience
projects.realWorldUsage: Used on Gaurav's portfolio for service offerings. Clients can browse mentorship, debugging help, resume review, and development services, then book and pay seamlessly.
projects.architecture: Frontend: Service listing and booking flows. Backend: Service management APIs, payment webhooks, ticket system. Database: MongoDB for all operational data.

projects.title: ZipLink
projects.summary: A full-stack URL shortener project built with Flask, SQLite, Tailwind CSS, and Jinja2. Automatically generates collision-resistant short codes, redirects users to target destinations, and tracks click counts via a unified dashboard.

highlights: Short URL creation with collision-resistant codes
Visit tracking and click counters in SQLite
Dashboard for link listing and deletion

projects.title: InstaX
projects.summary: High-performance social media platform built using Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, TypeScript, Prisma ORM, Neon PostgreSQL, Clerk OAuth, and UploadThing edge storage. Features optimistic client updates, drag-and-drop media uploads, and real-time-like notifications.
projects.problem: Modern social media interfaces suffer from laggy feedback, database bottlenecks, unoptimized assets causing visual layouts shifts, and complex client-server synchronization challenges that degrade user experiences.
highlights: Media uploads powered by UploadThing edge CDN
Optimistic UI updates for likes and comments
Prisma database queries on Neon serverless PostgreSQL
Real-time-like notification hub and follower counts

faq.question: What technologies do you use?
faq.answer: I mainly work with React and JavaScript for frontend development, Node.js and Express for backend APIs, Python for AI/ML and data work, and MongoDB for databases. I'm also experienced with authentication (JWT), real-time communication (Socket.IO), payment processing (Stripe, Cashfree), and AI integration (DeepSeek API).

faq.question: Are you available for internships or freelance work?
faq.answer: Yes, I'm actively open to internships, entry-level developer roles, freelance projects, remote work, and collaborations. I'm flexible with remote, hybrid, or on-site setups. You can reach out through the contact page or book a mentorship session to discuss opportunities.

faq.question: What kind of projects have you built?
faq.answer: I've built full-stack applications including a dynamic portfolio platform with payments and chatbot integration, real-time chat applications with Socket.IO, service platforms with booking systems, hostel management systems, certificate verification platforms, and AI/computer vision prototypes in Python. Most of my projects are publicly available on GitHub.

faq.question: Can you help beginners with web development?
faq.answer: Yes, absolutely. I offer mentorship, debugging help, resume reviews, and guidance for beginners getting into web development. My approach is practical and build-first - I believe in learning by shipping real projects rather than staying in tutorials. I'm open to helping students with project guidance and concepts.

faq.question: How can I contact you or book your services?
faq.answer: You can reach me through several ways: 1) Visit the contact page on my portfolio for direct messaging, 2) Book services like mentorship, debugging, or resume review directly on the portfolio, 3) Connect with me on LinkedIn at linkedin.com/in/ggauravky, 4) Check out my GitHub at github.com/ggauravky, or 5) Email me at kumar.gaurav.yadav2007@gmail.com.

faq.question: What is your approach to learning and growth?
faq.answer: I follow a build-first mentality. Instead of staying in tutorials, I learn concepts and immediately apply them to real projects. I ship publicly, document my work, and iterate based on feedback. I focus on consistent daily progress through DSA practice, structured learning, and building real systems rather than irregular bursts of effort.

faq.question: What makes you different from other developers?
faq.answer: My strongest differentiators are: 1) Consistency - I don't rely on motivation, I build discipline and routine, 2) Public proof of work - all my projects are shipped and documented, 3) Build-first mindset - I learn by creating real systems, not just studying, 4) Full-stack capability - I can handle frontend, backend, databases, and AI integration end-to-end.

faq.question: What's your strongest project and why?
faq.answer: One of my strongest projects is the Real-Time Chat Application because it combines multiple complex systems: JWT-based authentication, Socket.IO for real-time messaging, MongoDB for persistence, Cloudinary for media uploads, and a polished React frontend. It taught me about async state management, event-driven architecture, and production-style full-stack engineering.

faq.question: What are you currently learning?
faq.answer: I'm currently focused on Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA), advanced AI/ML concepts, MERN stack scalability and optimization, system design fundamentals, and building production-oriented projects that can scale.

faq.question: What kind of team environment do you prefer?
faq.answer: I prefer learning-focused and fast-moving teams that value: 1) Ownership and autonomy, 2) Clean engineering and code quality, 3) Experimentation and iteration, 4) Continuous improvement, 5) Clear communication and documentation. I work best in environments where the team cares about growth and shipping quality work.
